findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make reserve() atomically PERSIST the estimate (append a pending/reserved row) so an in-flight or not-yet-finalized run's estimate counts toward `spent`, and reconcile replaces the estimate with actual spend on finalize; specify how concurrent reserve() calls are serialized (e.g. file lock).
evidence: Plan: `ledger.reserve(estimate)` refuses when `spent + estimate > cap - reserve`
Plan: 'on completion the rows are priced and the ledger row finalised with actual spend' - spent is only known post-run
No pending/reservation row is written at reserve() time, so concurrent or overlapping runs share a stale `spent`
Epic runs multiple Tier-1/Tier-2 commissioning runs (AC1), making overlap realistic
findings.finding: reserve() is a check-then-act race: `spent` is only updated when a run finalizes, and the plan never persists a reservation between the pre-flight check and finalization, so two runs launched before the first finalizes both read the same `spent`, both pass `spent + estimate > cap - reserve`, and combined exceed the $200 cap.
scenarios: Two eval runs started back-to-back before the first finalizes both pass reserve() and together exceed the cap
A long agentic run is in flight (not yet finalized) while a second run's pre-flight reads spent as if the first cost $0
findings.suggested_fix: On reserve(), append a `status=reserved` row carrying the estimate under a file lock; sum `usd` of finalized rows PLUS `estimate` of still-reserved rows when computing `spent`; on finalize/reconcile, flip the row to `status=finalized` with actual usd.

findings.finding: The plan asserts genai-prices will price 'the pinned Bedrock model ids' for pre-flight estimation, but does not verify that those specific pinned ids actually RESOLVE in genai-prices, nor guard the estimate against the silent-unpriced path — the same failure the existing _pricing_model_ref documents (bug 2ca9): calc_price raises LookupError for an unresolved model and the caller returns None (unpriced). A pre-flight estimate built on that path would silently yield $0 for an unresolvable id and ALWAYS pass the cap check, defeating the refuse-over-cap guarantee.
findings.location: Approach — Pre-flight bullet; 'Assume genai-prices Bedrock ids as the price source'
scenarios: A pinned Bedrock model id (e.g. anthropic.claude-*-v1:0 form) is not present in the bundled genai-prices data at run time; the pre-flight estimate silently computes $0 and the run proceeds past the $200 cap it was meant to enforce.
findings.suggested_fix: In the pre-flight path, price a Usage for each pinned id and treat a None/LookupError result as a hard error (refuse the run with a clear message naming the unresolved id), never as $0; add a unit test asserting an unresolvable model id is refused, not admitted.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how concurrent reserve/finalise against the single ledger.jsonl is serialized (file lock / atomic reserve-then-write, or a documented single-runner assumption) so two in-flight runs cannot each pass the cap check and jointly exceed $200.
evidence: 'ledger.reserve(estimate) refuses ... when spent + estimate > cap − reserve'
'every eval run opens a usage-log session ... on completion the rows are priced and the ledger row finalised'
ABSENCE: no lock, atomic append, or ownership rule for concurrent reserve/finalise against the single committed ledger file
findings.finding: The committed ledger.jsonl is shared state read then written by reserve() (spent + estimate > cap - reserve), but the plan defines no concurrency control for two eval runs that reserve concurrently — both read the same `spent`, both pass the cap check, and both proceed, so the $200 cap can be exceeded by the sum of two in-flight runs (check-then-act TOCTOU).
findings.suggested_fix: Have reserve() record a pending reservation row (estimate) inside a file-locked read-modify-write, so `spent` includes outstanding reservations; finalise reconciles the reservation to actual spend.
